answer: A time-locked onyx vault resists Sybil attacks like this: a new identity must first complete verifiable work and lock that credential in the vault for several epochs before it can grade or vote. It can still do ordinary work, but influence is delayed. An attacker who spawns thousands of identities faces a ripple of waiting periods: each fake identity must separately earn and wait, so influence cannot be bought instantly by mass creation, and any early dishonesty forfeits the locked credential before it ever pays off.
